transcript: Birdie
Hi! I help businesses figure out exactly what they need from a chatbot. Before we start — what's your name?
Bernadette "Bernie" Fontaine

Oh hi there sweetie! I'm Bernie, well Bernadette really but nobody's called me that since my mother was alive God rest her soul, she used to say "Bernadette Marie" when I was in trouble ha! Anyways everybody just calls me Bernie, I run Bernie's Sweet Somethings out of my kitchen here just outside Scranton, been doing it eleven years now ever since I retired from teaching fourth grade, oh I miss those little rascals sometimes but not the grading let me tell you, my hip wasn't too happy standing at that chalkboard all day anyway lol. So yes! Bernie's my name, cakes are my game as my grandson says, he's the one who plays baseball, wait did I already tell you about his game last week? Anyway what were we talking about, oh right you wanted my name, it's Bernie :)
Birdie

It's so nice to meet you, Bernie! Eleven years of baking cakes sounds wonderful — and I bet your grandson's baseball games are a nice break from the kitchen. So tell me, what's the main thing you're hoping a chatbot could help you with in the bakery business?
Bernadette "Bernie" Fontaine

Oh bless you for asking, honey! Well let me think here, um, oh gosh where do I even start— you know funny you should mention the baseball games because just last week my grandson Tyler hit a double and I about spilled my iced tea I was so excited, his coach is this real nice young man, reminds me of my Ashley's husband actually, oh Ashley's my granddaughter who helps me with deliveries on the weekends bless her heart, she's got her own car now so that's been a big help because my hip's been acting up something fierce and I can't be running boxes up and down porch steps like I used to, especially since that time the Hendersons had all them icy steps and I about went down like a sack of potatoes with a red velvet in my arms, oh Lord that would've been a mess.

But anyway! What I really need help with, I think, is people keep texting me at all hours asking "how much is a cake" and honey I just — I never know what to tell them right off the bat because it really depends on the design you know, like if it's just a plain two layer that's one thing but if somebody wants some big fondant unicorn thing that's a whole different story, I kinda have to see a picture first before I can even guess a price. And also I get folks asking can I make it for tomorrow and I have to explain no no no I need at least five days, preferably two weeks if it's something fancy, my oven's old as dirt bless its heart and I can only get so many big orders done in a week anyhow. So maybe something that helps answer those two things without me having to type it all out every single time on my phone, my thumbs get so tired!
Birdie

That makes so much sense, Bernie — those two questions alone must eat up your whole day! Let's start with the pricing piece. For a simple, plain two-layer cake with no fancy design, what do you usually charge — like a starting price or range?
Bernadette "Bernie" Fontaine

Oh that one I actually DO know off the top of my head, ha, it's the fancy ones that trip me up! A plain two layer 8 inch cake, nothing crazy, just good frosting and maybe a simple little message on top, that's $55. That's been my price for a while now, though my niece keeps telling me "Aunt Bernie you're too cheap" but I don't know, I don't wanna price out the nice families, you know like the Petrocellis, they get a cake from me every single year for their little girl's birthday and she's got the same order every time, chocolate cake vanilla frosting, sweet as pie that one.

Now if we're talkin cupcakes that's $28 a dozen, and my cannoli trays, oh those fly off the counter around the holidays, that's $65 for two dozen. But the second somebody says "can you make it look like a castle" or "can it have my dog's face on it" — that's where my brain just goes blank on pricing, honey, I really do have to see what they want first, it starts around $120 for anything fondant or sculpted but truly it depends, some of these Pinterest pictures people bring me, Lord have mercy, I saw one lady want a five tier topsy turvy cake and I said honey that's not a birthday cake that's a science project ha!

Anyway yes — $55 flat for the basic one, that part's easy!
Birdie

Got it, Bernie — $55 for the basic cake, $28 a dozen for cupcakes, and $65 for two dozen cannoli, that's easy to remember! Now, do cupcakes and cannoli trays need that same 5-day notice, or can you usually whip those up faster?
Bernadette "Bernie" Fontaine

Oh honey good question! Truth be told cupcakes and the cannoli trays I can usually turn around a little quicker than the big cakes, especially the cannoli since that's really just assembly, shells and filling, I don't even have to bake anything for those except maybe a day ahead for freshness, but I still like to have at LEAST a couple days notice, three's better, because you would not believe how many people want cannoli trays the same week as Christmas or Easter, oh Lord, one year I had four people all want trays the same Saturday before Easter and I about lost my mind, Ashley had to help me box them up at midnight, we were laughing so hard we were slap happy tired.

Cupcakes same kinda thing, if it's just a simple dozen with regular frosting I can sometimes do it in a day or two if my week's not already packed, but honey I can only handle about four big orders a week total between everything, my kitchen's just me and my old oven bless its heart, so if someone calls me on a Wednesday wanting cupcakes for Friday I gotta check my book first before I say yes. So I guess the real answer is — 5 days is still my safe rule for anything, but I CAN sometimes squeeze in cupcakes or cannoli faster if I'm not already booked up, it just depends on the week, kinda like the whole pricing thing ha, everything with me is "it depends" isn't it, my niece says I should just make a sign that says that ha!
Birdie

That makes sense, Bernie, sounds like your book fills up fast around the holidays! Let's switch gears a bit — when someone does order, how do they usually pay you? Cash, card, Venmo, something like that?
Bernadette "Bernie" Fontaine

Oh honey, easy one! I do half down when they order, either Venmo or cash, whichever's easier for them, and then the rest they pay when they come pick it up, I don't do no cards, I looked into one of them little square readers a couple years back but honey the fees just about made my head spin and I said forget it, cash and Venmo's worked for eleven years I don't need to fix what ain't broken.

Speaking of Venmo though, oh Lord, I had the funniest thing happen, this nice young fella ordered a groom's cake shaped like a fishing boat if you can believe that, and he went and sent the Venmo payment to some other "Bernie" in Ohio or somewhere, poor thing, we had to sort that whole mess out over the phone while I was standing in my kitchen with flour up to my elbows, Ashley thought it was hilarious, she said "Grandma you're famous in Ohio now" ha!

But yes — half down, Venmo or cash, rest on pickup, that's how I keep it simple for myself, my brain can't be doing invoices and all that fancy stuff at my age.
Birdie

Ha, famous in Ohio, I love that! Okay Bernie, one more money question — if someone needs to cancel an order, or doesn't come pick it up after paying their deposit, what happens? Do you have a rule for that, or do you just handle it case by case?
Bernadette "Bernie" Fontaine

Oh gosh, honey, that's a good question and if I'm bein honest I don't really have like a official RULE written down anywhere, I kinda just handle it as it comes, case by case like you said. Most people are so sweet about it, like if somebody's grandma passed or their kid got the chicken pox right before the birthday party, Lord love em, I usually just work with em, maybe hold their deposit for a different date or somethin.

Now I did have ONE time, oh this is a story, this woman ordered a big ol sheet cake for her office Christmas party and then just never came to get it, never called, nothin, and I was standing here Thursday with this beautiful poinsettia cake just sittin there and I thought well shoot now what do I do with this, Ashley ended up bringing half of it to Tyler's baseball team bless her heart, they ate good that day ha!

But to answer you proper, no I don't think I got a real policy, I just kinda go with my gut and my heart on it, my niece keeps telling me "Aunt Bernie you need rules or people will walk all over you" and she's probably right, that's maybe somethin I should figure out better, huh.
Birdie

That's alright, Bernie, lots of small business owners are in the same boat — we can just note that as something still being figured out. Let's talk about your hours — what days and times are you actually available for people to reach you, place orders, or pick up cakes?
Bernadette "Bernie" Fontaine

Oh sure thing honey! So I bake Tuesday through Friday, that's my kitchen time, gotta have my coffee and my little radio going, I listen to that oldies station while I mix, and pickups are Thursday Saturday 10 to 4, that gives me a little wiggle room to finish things up before folks come knocking. Sundays and Mondays I'm closed closed CLOSED, that's church day and then family day, my whole brood comes over Monday nights for dinner, well most Mondays, unless Tyler's got a game then we're all down at the field instead eating hot dogs instead of my cooking ha!

I don't really answer texts at like 11 o'clock at night neither, my niece set my phone up so it does that little "do not disturb" thing overnight bless her, cause I used to just answer everybody right away even at Midnight and my husband God rest him used to say "Bernadette put the phone down" ha! So yeah — Tuesday to Friday for the baking and orders, Thursday Saturday 10 to 4 for pickup, closed Sunday Monday. That's been my rhythm for eleven years now and it works for me, keeps me sane, well as sane as I get anyway!
Birdie

Got it — Tuesday to Friday baking, Thursday and Saturday 10 to 4 for pickup, closed Sunday and Monday. Now, when people reach out to you, is it always by text message, or do folks also message you on Facebook, Instagram, or anywhere else?
Bernadette "Bernie" Fontaine

Oh honey, mostly it's text, everybody's just got my cell number from word of mouth or my little business cards I leave at the Petrocelli's deli counter, they let me put a little stack right by the register bless them. But I do got a Facebook page too, my niece set that up for me oh must be five six years ago now, "Bernie's Sweet Somethings" it's called, same as the business, and people message me on there sometimes through the Messenger thing, pictures of cakes they like and whatnot, Pinterest pictures too, lord the Pinterest pictures never end ha!

I tried the Instagram for about a hot minute, Ashley kept telling me "Grandma you gotta post reels" and I don't even know what a reel IS honey, I posted like six pictures of finished cakes and then just kind of forgot about it, my thumbs aren't fast enough for all that, between that and Facebook and just plain old texting it's a lot to keep track of for one old lady with a hip that don't work right ha. Oh and sometimes people just call me too, actually call and talk like a real phone call, mostly my older customers, the young ones never call, they'd rather text a book report than pick up the phone ha!

But yeah I'd say it's mostly texting, then Facebook messenger second, and every once in a while an actual phone call. That's probably part of why things get so jumbled up for me, everything's coming at me different ways all day long.
Birdie

Oh that Pinterest problem sounds so real, ha! Okay, you mentioned checking 'your book' to see if you're already booked up for the week — is that a paper calendar, a notebook, an app, something like that? I want to understand how you keep track of orders.
Bernadette "Bernie" Fontaine

Oh that "book" honey, ha, makes it sound so official don't it, it's just this beat up ol' spiral notebook I keep on the kitchen counter, corner's all stained with vanilla extract from I don't even know when, my son got me a fancy planner one Christmas thinking he was helping and honey it's still got the plastic wrap on it in a drawer somewhere, I just never took to it, I like my messy notebook, I write the customer's name, what they ordered, when it's due, and a little check mark when they pay their deposit, sometimes there's a coffee ring right over somebody's order and I gotta squint real hard to remember whose cake that even was ha!

Ashley's been on me for two years now saying "Grandma you need this on your phone" and there's some app she keeps showing me, calendar this calendar that, but honey between you and me I get a little nervous pushing too many buttons, I'm afraid I'll delete somebody's whole wedding order by accident and then where would I be, standing in my kitchen crying into a bowl of buttercream, no thank you! So yes — paper notebook, kitchen counter, right by the phone, that's my whole "system" ha, not fancy but it's worked eleven years so far, knock on wood, well knock on my old wooden counter I guess!
Birdie

That notebook sounds like it's been a trusty little sidekick for eleven years, ha! Okay Bernie, roughly how many messages or calls would you say you get in a typical week asking about cakes — even a rough guess is fine?
Bernadette "Bernie" Fontaine

Oh gosh, honey, let me think here... probably, oh I don't know, maybe fifteen twenty messages a week? Sometimes more if it's near a holiday or wedding season, Lord have mercy in May and June my phone just about explodes with all the wedding cake questions, and then there's the birthday ones which come in steady all year round cause birthdays don't care what season it is ha! Some weeks it's quiet, maybe just five six people checkin in, and then BAM other weeks I got twenty five messages and three phone calls and somebody's cousin messaging me on the Facebook too all in like two days, it's never real predictable, kinda like my hip, some days it don't bother me a bit and other days I can barely get up off the porch step ha!

I'd say average week, just guessing here, probably somewhere around fifteen to twenty folks reaching out one way or another, and out of all of those maybe only, oh I don't know, six or seven actually turn into real orders, the rest are just people askin questions or lookin at pictures and never following up, which is fine by me honestly, keeps me from gettin too overwhelmed since I can only do them four big orders a week anyway, my oven and my back can only take so much ha!
Birdie

That's really helpful, Bernie, thank you! Now, for the custom cakes where you need to actually see a picture before quoting — when the bot gets one of those requests, should it just tell the customer 'Bernie will get back to you with a price,' and then it comes straight to your phone? Or is there someone else, like Ashley, who should be looped in for that?
Bernadette "Bernie" Fontaine

Oh no honey, that one's all me, Ashley bless her heart she just does the deliveries on the weekends, driving the boxes around, she don't know nothin about pricing or fondant or none of that, she'd probably just tell em "call my grandma" ha! So yeah whatever the bot does, it oughta just come straight to my phone, that's the only way it works, I'm the one who's gotta squint at the Pinterest picture and figure out if it's a $120 job or a $250 "oh Lord what did I get myself into" job, if you know what I mean.

Now don't get me wrong Ashley's a smart girl, she's the one who set up my Facebook years ago and she's always trying to teach me new things on my phone, bless her patience, but the actual cake decisions, the pricing, all that creative stuff, that's gotta come to me, I'm the one standing there with the frosting bag in my hand ha! So I guess the bot could just say somethin like "Bernie will look at your picture and get back to you with a price" and then however that message gets to me, phone notification or whatever you got planned, that's how it oughta work. Ashley's just my delivery girl and my technology helper, not my business partner, though sometimes she acts like she wants to be ha, she's got big ideas that one, reminds me of her mother.
Birdie

That's really clear, Bernie, thank you. Now let's talk about what kind of bot fits you best — some folks want a full booking system where customers can pick dates and pay right in the chat, others just want something simpler that answers the common questions and sends the request to you to handle personally, like you've described. Given how you like to keep things simple, which sounds more like what you want?
Bernadette "Bernie" Fontaine

Oh honey, definitely the simpler one, no question about it! I get nervous enough with my phone as it is, remember I told you about that fancy planner my son got me still sittin in the drawer with the plastic wrap on it, ha, well that's exactly what would happen if you gave me some big fancy booking system, I'd just stare at it and go back to my notebook out of pure fright! 

I don't need people pickin dates and payin right there in the chat and all that, honey, that sounds like a whole lotta buttons for me to mess up, I'd probably approve somebody for a Tuesday when I don't even bake Tuesdays for pickup or something crazy like that. I just need somethin that can answer the easy stuff, you know, like "we're closed Sunday Monday" or "cupcakes are $28 a dozen" or "Bernie needs at least 5 days notice," that kinda thing, and then for the picture stuff and the real pricing and all that, just send it on over to me and I'll handle it myself like I always do, squinting at my phone with flour on my fingers ha!

Keep it simple sweetie, that's kinda my whole philosophy, simple recipes, simple system, less chance of me burning something down ha! My niece is probably gonna roll her eyes at me for sayin that but honey it's worked for eleven years, don't need to reinvent the whole cake now.
Birdie

Simple it is, Bernie — that fits you perfectly. Last couple of things: should the bot have a friendly, warm personality kind of like you, and would you like it to have a name, or just introduce itself as being from Bernie's Sweet Somethings?
Bernadette "Bernie" Fontaine

Oh honey, warm and friendly, yes yes, absolutely, none of that stiff robot talk, I want it soundin like somebody's sweet auntie answerin the phone, not like one of them automated voices that says "press one for English" ha, drives me up a wall when I call the electric company and get stuck in that maze of button pressin, I just want to talk to a PERSON, well I guess in this case a person-ish bot, ha!

As for a name, oh gosh, I hadn't even thought about that, my mind goes right to my grandkids' names, or ooh what if we called it somethin cute like "Sprinkles" or "Frosty" — no wait Frosty sounds like a snowman not a cake ha — or maybe just somethin simple like "Bernie's Helper" so people know it's connected to me and my shop, don't need to get too clever about it, I'm not real fancy if you haven't noticed by now ha! Actually you know what, my late husband used to call me "Bernie B" sometimes, kinda cute, maybe somethin like that? But truly honey whatever you think works best, you're the expert here, I trust you, just as long as it don't sound too much like a robot and more like it's got a little warmth to it, like it just pulled a tray of cookies outta the oven, ha! I'm all for whatever keeps it feelin homey and not too corporate, this is a home kitchen business after all, not some big fancy factory, lord no.
Birdie

Aww, 'Bernie B' is so sweet, I love that — we'll pass along your name ideas to the build team so they can land on something warm like that. Just one more quick thing: will all your customers be messaging in English, or do you get folks texting you in other languages too, like Spanish?
Bernadette "Bernie" Fontaine

Oh good question honey! No, far as I can recall it's all been English, everybody around here just texts me regular English, I did have a real sweet couple a couple years back, the Ramirez family I think it was, lovely people ordered a quinceañera cake for their daughter gorgeous thing with the fondant flowers all cascading down, but even they texted me in English, no problem there. So no I don't think you gotta worry about no other languages for me honey, just plain English, which is good cause lord knows I only ever learned the one language good enough to spell it ha, my French comes out sounding like a chicken clucking my niece says!
Birdie

Good to know, plain English keeps it simple! One last open question before I wrap up, Bernie — is there anything else on your mind about pricing, policies, or the business in general that you think would be helpful for me to know?
Bernadette "Bernie" Fontaine

Oh honey let me think... OH WAIT yes, I almost forgot the big one, my kitchen is NOT nut free, I gotta make sure that's real clear to folks cause I do use walnuts and almond stuff sometimes in my baking and I don't want nobody with a bad allergy getting hurt, that would just break my heart into a million pieces, so if the bot can just say somethin like "Bernie's kitchen isn't nut-free" right up front that would be a load off my mind, my niece is always after me about that, "Aunt Bernie you gotta put that in writing everywhere" she says.

Oh and delivery too, I should mention, I really don't deliver, only if it's like ten minutes away and even then only if my hip's not actin up that day, ha, most the time I just tell folks to come on by for pickup Thursday or Saturday, Ashley does help with some Saturday deliveries but that's more for my regulars, not somethin I advertise real loud.

Oh and one more thing, and honey I probably shoulda mentioned this a while back but it just popped in my head, I'm not even real sure if my little license covers me sellin over at the farmers market two towns over, I been meanin to call the county about that for, oh Lord, two years now I think, just never got around to it, so I probably shouldn't have the bot sayin anything about farmers markets till I get that sorted, don't want to get myself in trouble ha!

And I guess the last little thing, not really a policy just my own gripe, my oven's old as the hills and I'm saving up for a nice new double oven, so if orders ever slow down some week it's probably cause I'm prayin over that thing to just hold on a little longer ha! But that's probably more than you needed, that's about everything rattlin around in this old brain of mine honey!
Birdie

Oh that's really important, Bernie, thank you for catching all that! Let me read back everything I've got so you can make sure it's all correct:

**Services & Pricing:**
- Plain 2-layer 8-inch cake: $55 flat, 5 days notice
- Cupcakes: $28/dozen, usually 5 days notice (sometimes 1-2 days if not booked up)
- Cannoli trays: $65 for two dozen, usually 5 days notice (sometimes 2-3 days if not booked up)
- Custom/fondant cakes: starts around $120+, varies by design (needs a picture to quote), 2 weeks notice preferred

**Policies:**
- Payment: half down (cash or Venmo) at order, rest due at pickup; no cards
- No formal cancellation/no-show policy yet — handled case by case
- Capacity: about 4 big orders/week max
- Kitchen is NOT nut-free — walnuts/almonds used
- No regular delivery — pickup only (Thurs/Sat 10-4), rare close-by exceptions, Ashley helps some Saturdays for regulars
- Farmers market sales — not confirmed with the county yet, so the bot won't mention this at all

**Hours:** Bakes Tue-Fri, pickup Thu & Sat 10am-4pm, closed Sun/Mon, no overnight replies

**Channels:** Text (main), Facebook Messenger, phone calls — all in English

**Volume:** ~15-20 inquiries/week, 6-7 turn into orders, busier around holidays and wedding season

**Handoff:** Anything needing a custom price/picture goes straight to Bernie's phone — Ashley is delivery/tech only, not pricing

**Scope:** A simple bot — answers common questions (hours, prices, notice needed, nut warning) and routes anything custom straight to Bernie. No booking or payment system.

**Persona:** Warm and friendly, like a sweet auntie — name ideas floated were 'Bernie's Helper' or 'Bernie B,' final call left to the build team.

Does all that sound right to you, Bernie, or is there anything you want me to fix?
Bernadette "Bernie" Fontaine

Oh honey that all sounds just right to me, you did such a good job keepin all that straight, my head woulda been spinnin tryin to read all that back myself ha! Let me just squint at it here a second... nope, that's all correct as far as I can tell, the prices, the notice times, the nut thing, all of it, you got it all down perfect.

Oh except honey one little thing, you said cupcakes and cannoli "usually 5 days notice" but I think what I meant was 5 days is my SAFE rule but I really can squeeze em in faster sometimes if my week's not full, which I think you already got in there too actually, so maybe that's not even a mistake, just me bein confusin as usual, my niece says I could confuse a compass ha!

But other than my own ramblin, no, that's all spot on sweetie, you're real good at this, you shoulda been one of my students, you'd have gotten a gold star for sure. Thank you for bein so patient with an old lady who can't answer a question without tellin you three stories first ha!
Birdie

Ha, you'd have been one of my favorite students too, Bernie! Thank you so much for all your time and stories today, they made this a real joy. I've got everything written down clearly now, and this will get passed along to the team who'll actually build your bot. No promises on exact dates from me, but you're in good hands. Take care of that hip, and give Tyler a high five for his double for me!

brief.business_description: Bernie runs a home-based bakery, Bernie's Sweet Somethings, just outside Scranton, PA. She's been doing it for eleven years after retiring from teaching fourth grade. Her granddaughter Ashley helps with weekend deliveries (for regulars only, not widely advertised) and technology; Ashley is not involved in pricing or cake decisions.
brief.problem_to_solve: Bernie gets texted at all hours with 'how much is a cake' and 'can you make it by tomorrow' questions, and typing out answers each time on her phone is tiring. She also gets messages via Facebook Messenger and phone calls, so inquiries come in through multiple channels and get jumbled. She wants the bot to help handle these common questions.
channels: Text/SMS (primary - most customers have her cell from word of mouth or business cards)
Facebook Messenger (page: 'Bernie's Sweet Somethings', set up ~5-6 years ago)
integrations: No digital system currently - Bernie tracks all orders in a paper spiral notebook on her kitchen counter (customer name, order, due date, deposit checkmark). She is hesitant about apps/digital tools, worried about accidentally deleting orders.
brief.conversation_volume: Roughly 15-20 inquiries per week on average (text, Messenger, calls combined), ranging from as few as 5-6 in slow weeks to 25+ near holidays/wedding season (May/June especially busy for wedding cakes). Of those, only about 6-7 per week typically convert into actual orders.
services_and_pricing: Plain two-layer 8-inch cake (basic design, simple message): $55 flat, needs at least 5 days notice (safe rule)
Cupcakes: $28 per dozen; 5 days is Bernie's safe standard answer, but she can often do it faster (1-2 days) if her week isn't already booked up

Cannoli trays: $65 per two dozen (popular around holidays); 5 days is Bernie's safe standard answer, but she can often do it faster (2-3 days) if her week isn't already booked up - it's assembly only, no baking required except a day ahead for freshness

Custom/fondant/sculpted cakes (e.g. shaped like a castle, dog's face, etc.): starts around $120 but varies significantly - Bernie needs to see a picture/design before quoting exact price; prefers 2 weeks notice for fancy custom work
faq_answers: Pricing depends on design - a plain two-layer cake is priced differently than a custom fondant design; Bernie needs to see a picture before she can quote exact price for custom work.

Lead time: 5 days is Bernie's safe standard rule to quote customers for any order; custom/fancy work prefers 2 weeks; cupcakes/cannoli can often be done faster if her week isn't already booked, but 5 days is the safe answer to give.
Hours: Bakes Tuesday-Friday. Pickup available Thursday and Saturday, 10am-4pm. Closed Sunday and Monday (church and family day).
Allergy info: Bernie's kitchen is NOT nut-free - she uses walnuts and almond products sometimes. This should be stated clearly/upfront to customers.

Delivery: Bernie generally does not deliver - customers are directed to pick up Thursday or Saturday. Occasional exceptions for very close (10 min away) locations if her hip allows, and Ashley helps with some Saturday deliveries for regular customers only - this is not something advertised widely.
business_policies: Bernie can only handle about 4 big orders per week total across all order types, since it's just her and her oven (capacity constraint).
Holidays (Christmas, Easter) and wedding season (May/June) get very high demand, which strains her capacity.
Payment: half down at order time (cash or Venmo, whichever's easier for customer), remainder due at pickup. No card payments accepted (tried a Square reader before but fees were too high).

No formal cancellation/no-show policy exists yet - Bernie handles it case-by-case, often working with customers (e.g. holding deposit for a new date) for sympathetic situations. Had one no-show/uncollected order (a sheet cake) with no resolution process in place. Bernie acknowledges she may need a real policy but hasn't decided on one.
Bernie doesn't respond to texts overnight - phone is set to Do Not Disturb (set up by her niece) since she used to answer at all hours.
Order tracking is entirely on paper (spiral notebook) - no digital record currently.
Kitchen is not nut-free (uses walnuts/almond products) - important allergy disclosure.
No standard delivery service - pickup only, with rare informal exceptions for very close/regular customers.
Bernie is not certain her license covers selling at a farmers market two towns over (hasn't confirmed with the county) - bot should NOT mention or offer farmers market info until this is resolved.
escalation_rules: For custom/fondant/design cake pricing requests (anything needing a picture to quote), the bot should tell the customer something like 'Bernie will look at your picture and get back to you with a price,' and route the inquiry/notification straight to Bernie's phone - not to Ashley. Ashley only handles deliveries and tech setup, not pricing or cake decisions.
open_items: Bernie doesn't have a formal cancellation/no-show/deposit-forfeiture policy - she handles it case by case and hasn't decided if/how she wants the bot to state a policy.
Bot name - leaning toward something warm/simple like 'Bernie's Helper' or 'Bernie B' but open to suggestion, not fully decided.
Farmers market sales - Bernie hasn't confirmed with the county if her license covers it, so bot should avoid the topic entirely for now.
additional_notes: Bernie's hip issues limit her ability to do deliveries herself; granddaughter Ashley handles some weekend deliveries for regulars.
Bernie has been told by her niece she may be underpricing but is hesitant to raise prices for loyal repeat customers (e.g. the Petrocelli family who order the same cake every year).
A customer once accidentally Venmo'd a different 'Bernie' in Ohio instead of her - had to sort out over the phone.
Bernie's niece has told her she needs clearer rules/policies so people don't take advantage.
Bernie is nervous about complex apps/technology, worried about accidentally deleting important order info.
Bernie confirmed she wants a simple bot (FAQ answers + routing to her for anything needing pricing judgment), not a full booking/payment app.

Bot persona: warm, friendly, like a sweet auntie - not robotic or corporate. Bernie likes name ideas like 'Bernie's Helper' or 'Bernie B' (a nickname her late husband used) but leaves final call to the build team.
Bernie's oven is old and she's saving for a new double oven; occasional slower weeks may be due to equipment strain/limits, not lack of demand.
